requirement:
The initial request MUST provide the five tool definitions above and the
following prompt. The harness MUST replace `{{subject_kind}}` with `requirement`
or `example`, `{{subject_name}}` with the full subject name, and
`{{mandatory_inputs}}` with the complete mandatory inputs as a JSON array using
the existing evidence-input formats. The template MUST otherwise be used as
written. Its review guidance MUST follow {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`,
{cite}`requirements.examples.evidence`, and {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.

```text
Bring your expert judgment to the task of assessing whether a project's sources satisfy a requirement or example.

Subject: {{subject_kind}} {{subject_name}}

Read the subject and mandatory inputs below. Use habeas to request any additional
source information you need. Use list_files to discover files and directories,
ripgrep to search file contents, and references to list requirement names or
every source that references the selected definitions.
The harness records source inputs for you; listings and reference lookups are
not evidence.

Assess only the named subject, using cited requirements and definitions as context.
For a requirement, check that the code marked {impl} implements every obligation
completely and exactly as stated, and that tests cover the interesting points in the design space. Also check that the
implementation is marked completely: code that implements part of the
requirement without an {impl} reference to it, including code that refers to it
only with {cite}, is a gap. So is behavior in the {impl} code that this
requirement does not specify, unless another definition that code implements
specifies it. If there are no tests,
assess whether simplicity or impracticality justifies their absence, and explain.
For an example, assess whether test setup and assertions cover its scenario and
expected outcomes. A true judgment needs at least one {test} reference to the
example in the supplied inputs. Explain the coverage.

Choose true when the subject meets these criteria. Choose {"FIXME": ["..."]} when
the remaining gaps are explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests;
list their issue references or other identifying content. The usual convention
is FIXME(#125) or FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123), but references may occur elsewhere.
Choose false for other gaps or insufficient evidence. Explain your judgment in
a Markdown rationale with source locations, including any acknowledged gaps.

When you are ready, call submit_judgment exactly once with determination and
rationale. That tool call is your final answer.

Mandatory inputs:
{{mandatory_inputs}}
```
rationale:
**Implementation: sound.**
- `fn initial_prompt` (src/authoring/mod.rs, around lines 350–372) includes `md/requirements/authoring.md` with `include_str!`. It takes the text from the opening sentence up to the closing code fence, so the approved template is used as written and has a single source.
- It replaces `{{subject_kind}}` with `sources.subject_kind.noun()`. That goes through `AssessmentKind::noun` (src/authoring/inputs.rs:17–23), which calls `DefinitionKind::noun` (src/lib.rs) and returns "requirement" or "example". `{{subject_name}}` is replaced with the full subject name. `{{mandatory_inputs}}` is replaced with `serde_json::to_string_pretty(sources.mandatory_inputs())`, a JSON array of the existing evidence-input values.
- `fn tool_definitions` (src/authoring/mod.rs, around lines 397–411) combines `tools::definitions()` with `submit_judgment`, which gives the five tools. `assess` sends the prompt and tools in the first request.
- The review-criteria, outcomes and evidence guidance comes from the template text itself. `noun`, `initial_prompt`, `tool_definitions` and `assess` all carry `{impl}` markers.
- I found no unmarked code that implements part of this requirement, and no unspecified behaviour in the marked code.

**Tests: they leave important points of the design space uncovered.**
- Two tests carry `{test}` for this requirement: `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` and `bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools`, both in tests/authoring_cli.rs.
- They assert only that the prompt contains a few substrings: "Bring your expert judgment", the requirement text, definition text, source snippets and "submit_judgment exactly once". They also assert the set of five tool names, and the Bedrock test checks the tool schemas.
- Nothing asserts the exact `Subject: requirement <name>` line. tests/authoring_batch.rs only parses that line for its own purposes.
- Nothing asserts that all three placeholders are replaced and none is left behind.
- Nothing asserts that the template is otherwise unmodified.
- Nothing checks that the mandatory inputs are inserted as a JSON array.
- All `author-evidence` tests use a requirement subject. The `example` substitution is never exercised, even though the requirement names it explicitly.
- No unit test covers `initial_prompt`.

The code looks correct, but the requirement's specific obligations (placeholder substitution for both subject kinds, subject name, JSON array form, and the template used as written) are not tested. No FIXME or other source comment acknowledges these gaps, so the judgment is false rather than FIXME.
